html:
SMTO-LLM-0070 — SMTO can't stop or restart a model server it doesn't control

GUID: 9d0ebb7f-68a8-5847-9015-30ced634d2f9
Slug: local-ai-runtime-not-owned
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO can only stop or restart model servers that the running Gateway started itself. It can't prove this one is its own, so it left it running to avoid interrupting someone else's work.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to stop or restart that model server using the computer's own tools. SMTO lost control of this server (for example when the Gateway restarted), so only someone on that computer can safely manage it.
  2. After they confirm it has stopped, ask SMTO in a new message to list the model servers on that Gateway and check it shows as stopped or exited. Starting a new copy while the old one still runs could make the two fight over the same port and graphics card.
  3. Then ask SMTO to start the model server again from your Local AI Runtime profile. A server SMTO starts itself can later be stopped and restarted from SMTO.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists a newly started model server for your profile, and stopping or restarting it from SMTO works.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't stop a process just because it uses the model server's port; it may belong to another program or person.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Stop/restart was refused because this Gateway has no live, SMTO-managed process handle for the runtime (restored after a Gateway restart, or an externally started server).

What this means

  • Stop/restart requires a retained managed-ownership record and live process handle; a restored manifest or external process does not supply that proof. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Stop/restart requires a retained managed-ownership record and live process handle; a restored manifest or external process does not supply that proof.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect ownership and the original runtime receipt; a PID or matching port alone is insufficient after Gateway replacement.

How to fix it

  • The runtime row has ownership other than smto_managed or no retained process handle, typically after the Gateway restarted and restored it as unknown ownership. Have the process's real owner stop or restart it with that host's own service tools, confirm it has exited, then start a fresh runtime from the accepted profile; never adopt or kill it by PID or port alone.
  • Ask the actual process owner to manage it; preserve unknown ownership and avoid adopting or killing by PID alone.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The control target has authoritative managed ownership, or its external owner confirms the intended lifecycle action independently.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
